name: Shelby GT500
description:
The 1967 Shelby GT500 represents the pinnacle of Carroll Shelby's collaboration with Ford, transforming the Mustang fastback into a high-performance street machine that combined raw American V8 power with legitimate handling dynamics. Following the success of the smaller-engined GT350, Shelby answered customer demands for more power by creating the GT500—a muscle car that could dominate both drag strips and road courses.

What set the GT500 apart from typical muscle cars was its comprehensive approach to performance. Beyond simply adding a bigger engine, Shelby transformed the entire car with upgraded suspension, improved brakes, a distinctive fiberglass hood with functional scoops, sequential tail lights, and aggressive racing stripes. The result was a car that looked fast standing still and delivered on every promise its appearance made.

Under the hood sat Ford's massive 428 cubic-inch (7.0L) Police Interceptor V8, officially rated at 360 horsepower and 569 Nm of torque—though many believe the true output was significantly higher, as Ford and Shelby often underrated their engines to satisfy insurance companies and racing homologation rules. The big-block V8 provided effortless torque across the rev range, delivering the GT500 from 0-100 km/h in just 6 seconds and pushing it to a top speed of 230 km/h.

The 1967 model year marked the final year of the classic, lean Shelby Mustangs before they grew larger and more luxurious in 1968. At 1,470 kg, the '67 GT500 offered an excellent power-to-weight ratio of 4.08 kg/hp, making it notably quicker than the heavier models that followed. This combination of manageable size, serious power, and Shelby's performance tuning created a car that was equally capable carving through mountain roads or launching down the quarter-mile.

The 1967 GT500 has become one of the most desirable classic American muscle cars, immortalized in films like 'Gone in 60 Seconds' (as 'Eleanor') and representing the golden era when Carroll Shelby was personally involved in creating street Mustangs. Today, it stands as the definitive example of what happens when a racing legend applies his expertise to a production muscle car—the result is a machine that transcends the muscle car formula to become a genuine American performance icon.
